title: Regional Model Adoption Likelihood Grid & Triggered Research Plan
creator: Evelyn Chen
description:
Problem: Sales and partnerships teams lack an operationalized way to anticipate which open or third-party models are likely to be adopted rapidly in a given region (NA / EU / APAC). This means we under-provision Dedicated capacity in the right regions and lag on pre-onboarding required quantization/hardware profiles.

Goal: Produce an Adoption Likelihood Grid (ALG) that scores model+region combinations weekly and wires in triggered research playbooks when signals cross thresholds. The ALG should combine external indicators (public release cadence, GitHub momentum, benchmark listings), telemetry signals (customer trial volume, token mix, latency preferences), and commercial signals (pricing changes, partner announcements).

Scope:
- Define signal taxonomy and scoring rules for a 3x3 likelihood x impact grid per region.
- Build a small ETL to ingest weekly signals from model-scout pipeline, telemetry dashboards, and public scraping.
- Prototype a simple dashboard (Confluence + Looker/Metabase draft) showing top-10 high-likelihood candidates per region.
- Author triggered research playbooks (technical compatibility checklist, quantization effort estimate, infra cost delta estimate, go/no-go handoff) that kick off when a model-region score > threshold.

Out of scope for this ticket: full productionization of routing automation and automated capacity provisioning (those will be follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: ALG scoring spec doc published and reviewed by Eng/Research/GT M (link in attachments)
Weekly ETL exports 6 baseline signals into a test dataset (public releases, GH stars, trial requests, embedding calls, pricing changes, partner press) for NA/EU/APAC
Prototype dashboard lists top-10 model-region scores and supports historical trend for 4 weeks
Three triggered research playbooks drafted and reviewed: low-effort compatibility probe, mid-effort quantization feasibility, high-effort enterprise readiness checklist
Handoff notes and a prioritized 90-day plan for Dedicated capacity pre-provisioning created and signed off by Infra PM
comments: 2025-02-06 Evelyn Chen: Scoped initial signal taxonomy with Research. Proposed weighting: 40% telemetry, 35% public momentum, 25% commercial. Asked Research to validate for bias vs smaller languages.
2025-02-12 Marco Diaz: Eng availability confirmed for a 2-sprint prototype ETL; will re-use the model-scout webhook. Need clarification on data retention for GH scrapes (legal).

2025-02-18 Research (Anita Rao): Ran quick backfill on 12 months of signals across 25 models; telemetry-only signal alone has 62% precision for short-term adoption in NA but degrades in APAC. Recommend region-specific thresholds.
2025-02-25 PM review (Gideon Morales): Adjusted scoring to include a volatility penalty for models with frequent breaking API changes. Added label 'pricing-economics'.

2025-03-03 Eng feedback (Priya Kumar): Prototype dashboard will use Metabase sandbox; we can expose CSV export for manual ops workflows. Raised concern about scraping latency for press signals — suggested use of RSS + partner monitoring instead.
2025-03-08 Legal (Samir Ahmed): OK to store public metadata and aggregate stats; do not store raw scraped full-text articles. Updated attachments with allowed endpoints.
2025-03-09 Evelyn Chen: Consolidated inputs, published draft ALG spec to Confluence, and requested review from Sales Eng and Partnerships for business-signal validation.
decision_log: Adopted weighted scoring (telemetry 40 / public momentum 35 / commercial 25) after Research showed better precision in NA; will keep region-specific thresholds to handle APAC variance.
Chose weekly cadence for signal refresh to balance noise vs agility; daily proved too noisy in backfill tests.
Triggered playbooks will be human-reviewed before any automated infra changes; automation is a follow-up after 2 successful handoffs.
Rejected immediate inclusion of raw news article content due to legal constraints; will use metadata/press mentions only.
